description.narrative: Oxfam’s New GINI program commences in April 2024 with pilot projects in Kenya, Colombia and Vietnam. The GINI program aims to support and influence work on inequality at the national level in the Global South. By collaborating with partners, the GINI program seeks to achieve both narrative and policy changes on various inequality issues in Vietnam and other pilot countries. In Vietnam, the program is titled the Global Inequality Influencing Program: Addressing Persisting Inequalities and Emerging Disparities in Vietnam (GINI-PIED). The program will support Vietnam in achieving its development priorities and the new national development agenda (named Vietnam’s Rising Era) after 2026 under the new leadership that focuses on strategic directions of social inclusion, environmental sustainability, and shared prosperity. The goal of the GINI-PIED program in Vietnam is to contribute evidence and innovative ideas to address persisting inequalities and emerging disparities as the country embarks on its ambitious Rising Era development agenda. Underthe Theory of Change of the New GINI Program in Vietnam with three outcomes, GINI-PIED Outcome 2 (that Oxfam plans to partner with the Ho Chi Minh National Academy of Politics) is to update Vietnam’s inequality evidence, insights, and documented innovations to highlight improvements, identify persisting inequalities, and uncover new areas of disparity that require innovative policy interventions. With robust research evidence, Oxfam will co-create new narratives and engagement strategies with various stakeholders, contributing to debates and knowledge beyond Vietnam, with relevance to other Global South contexts. This research report in the GINI-PIED project in Vietnam therefore aims to provide a comprehensive view ofVietnam’s evolving inequality landscape and identify emerging risks. As a flagship report, it will serve as a beacon of knowledge, contributing to GINI initiatives in various contexts. Additionally, it will offer new insights to inform future national andsub-national policy discussions and decision-making on inequalities. In addtion, this outcome includes activities of validating the research findings and updating the Human Economy framework for Vietnam through strategic engagement with think-tanks and national/sub-national government entities, notably Central Committee of Economy, TheInstitute for International Economics (Vietnam Academy of Social Sciences), sub-national research institutes etc. This justification specifies the rationale for and importance of the partnership with the Ho Chi Minh National Academy of Politics (HCMA) for Outcome2, to the exclusion of other organizations. Furthermore, it justifies the cost-effectiveness of the budget proposed by HCMA in relation to their designated expert roster
